facts.fact: GSMA states that the mobile Vital Records System, developed in 2010, enables births and deaths to be registered in health facilities and villages through a web-based app and mobile USSD; the document dates the system's use no more closely, so its publication date is used.

GSMA states that births and deaths are registered in health facilities and villages on the m-VRS by web-based app or mobile USSD, and that the information is then accessible to back-office registration officers, who verify the registration before approving the printing and issue of the birth certificate; no date is given for this, so the publication date is used.

systems.owner: Government of Uganda in a public-private partnership with Uganda Telecom (UTL), supported by UNICEF
systems.tiers: health facilities and villages; back-office registration officers verify

systems.system: National Identification Number issued to every child on registration of birth

systems.tiers: continuous registration; mass campaign 'My Country, My Identity' 2014-2016
